text: AdventureWorksDW2014 is already a genuinely well-built data warehouse, so this particular cleanup pass is noticeably lighter than Chapter Three's general Power Query lessons were — but lighter genuinely doesn't mean there's nothing real left to do here at all.

Three genuinely real tasks remain. First, decide for real, once and for all, which of Lesson 85's deliberately extra columns you're actually going to keep versus remove entirely. Second, rename raw warehouse column names into something clean enough that an actual report can display it directly to a non-technical viewer. And third, confirm every single date column — OrderDate, DueDate, ShipDate — genuinely loaded as a real Date type, not as plain text, which is a surprisingly common warehouse quirk worth double-checking rather than simply assuming.

One simple check catches most mistakes early, before they ever become a real problem down the line: renaming and removing columns should never, under any circumstance, change a table's actual row count. If a row count genuinely did change somewhere along the way, a stray filter step almost certainly snuck into your query steps without you ever noticing it happen.

Close and Apply commits every single one of these changes back into the real semantic model all at once, using the exact same schema-refresh mechanic Lesson 75 already described in detail. Lesson 87 is exactly where these newly cleaned tables actually become a genuine, working star schema for the very first time in this whole project.
